sections: Vault-first onboarding: one home for memory, provider secrets, and MCP wiring — better than pasting API keys into client config.

Run clawql init before connecting Cursor. Secrets live in
~/.ClawQL/vault/providers.json (same shape as HashiCorp
secret/clawql/providers). Memory tools use ~/.ClawQL/Memory/.
Default install loads the opinionated stack (Cloudflare, GitHub, Slack,
Linear, Notion, Onyx). Use CLAWQL_PROVIDER=all-providers only for every
bundled vendor plus Google top-50 and AWS top-50.
Restart Cursor or Claude Desktop after MCP config is written.

For agent-guided setup, copy the full prompt from the repo:
agent-setup-prompt.md
clawql onboard --interactive — init, write MCP config, smoke test
Or clawql init --interactive → mcp-config --write cursor → doctor --smoke
clawql secrets set <provider> — add keys without editing JSON
Smoke search + read-only execute on one default-stack vendor
Optional clawql init --push-vault when HashiCorp Vault is available (K8s)

| Mode            | Secrets store                                            |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Local stdio | ~/.ClawQL/vault/providers.json (loaded at MCP startup) |
| Kubernetes  | HashiCorp Vault → ESO → clawql-provider-env            |
| Dashboard   | Provider secrets UI → Vault KV                           |
The iOS app cannot run local stdio MCP or keep ~/.ClawQL on the device. Use Cursor Cloud Agents instead:
Dashboard Secrets — CLAWQL_HOME, CLAWQL_SYNC_*, bucket credentials, and provider API tokens (never in git or mcp.json).
stdio MCP in .cursor/mcp.json — npx -p clawql-mcp clawql-mcp; enable the clawql server when starting an agent run from iOS.
Team bucket — shared Memory/ via R2, S3, or GCS; end important runs with memory_sync { "direction": "auto" }.
Full walkthrough: cursor-ios-cloud-agent.md (also on the docs site at Cursor iOS + Cloud Agent).
